h1: [shocked, loud] There's a sea over Red Square! Right above the Kremlin!
h2: [smug, conspiratorial] Don't believe me? Let's rewind time!
c1: [dry, curious] Three hundred ten million years ago, a warm sea splashed right here.
c2: [proud] Its shells became white stone. They even named this age the Moscovian!
i1: [shivering, teeth chattering] Then a glacier came and dragged in boulders. One still sits in Kolomenskoye!
p1: [laughing, warm] Moscow's very first mention? A dinner invitation. One mighty dinner!
w1: [proud] Prince Dmitry Donskoy builds the Kremlin from white stone. That same sea stone!
r1: [sly, sarcastic] The red Kremlin was built by Italians. Then the tsar had it… whitewashed!
k1: [dry, sarcastic] They cast the Tsar Bell — two hundred tons! And it never rang once.
n1: [tense, low voice] Napoleon waited for the keys to Moscow. [smug] Nope — the city was empty and burning.
m1: [laughing, impressed] Mayakovskaya metro station won a Grand Prix — in New York!
t1: [warm, proud] Today thirteen million people live here. All walking on an ancient seabed!
x1: [playful, to the camera] Where to next? Drop a city — we'll rewind it!
